evidence: src/infrastructure/http/errorMiddleware.ts: STATUS_BY_KIND is the only place DomainErrorKind values are mapped to HTTP statuses, and errorMiddleware handles DomainError, BadRequestError and Express 4xx errors in one place

src/infrastructure/http/requestParsing.ts: BadRequestError, requireString, parsePlaceOrderBody and parseStatusBody hold all the request-shape checks; the comment says business validation stays in the domain
src/infrastructure/http/OrderController.ts: the place, listByState and advance handlers use parsePlaceOrderBody, requireString and parseStatusBody instead of checking inline
src/infrastructure/http/StockController.ts: has the same routes() and use-case delegation pattern as OrderController, with no separate error handling
Minor: the `!isRecord(body)` guard with the message 'Request body must be a JSON object' appears in both parsePlaceOrderBody and parseStatusBody, but it's a trivial guard, not a domain invariant
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All four files deal with one thing: the HTTP adapter. OrderController.ts and StockController.ts map routes to use cases. requestParsing.ts handles the shape checks on incoming requests. errorMiddleware.ts turns errors into HTTP responses.

Each rule lives in one place. The domain error-kind to status mapping exists only in errorMiddleware.ts (STATUS_BY_KIND). Shape validation exists only in requestParsing.ts, and its comment says business validation stays in the domain. BadRequestError is defined once and handled once.

The module's own abstractions are used consistently. OrderController calls parsePlaceOrderBody, parseStatusBody and requireString instead of checking request data inline. Neither controller catches errors itself; both leave that to the central middleware.

There is one small repetition: the check `!isRecord(body)` and its message appear in both parsePlaceOrderBody and parseStatusBody. It's a trivial guard, not a duplicated business rule, so it doesn't fail the rubric.
